title: Palindrome List
statement:
Decide whether a list of numbers reads the same forward and backward.

The first line is a whole number `n`. The second line holds `n` integers separated by single spaces. `n` is at least 1. Print `true` when the list is a palindrome and `false` otherwise. Check it by comparing the first item with the last, then the second with the second to last, moving inward from both ends. A list with one item is a palindrome.

Input:

```text
5
1 2 3 2 1
```

Expected output:

```text
true
```
hints: Keep two indexes, one starting at the front and one starting at the back.
Move them toward each other after each match. You can stop as soon as one pair differs, or when they meet.

python.solution:
def is_palindrome(items: list[int]) -> bool:
    left = 0
    right = len(items) - 1
    while left < right:
        if items[left] != items[right]:
            return False
        left += 1
        right -= 1
    return True


n = int(input())
items = [int(x) for x in input().split()]
print("true" if is_palindrome(items) else "false")
